minutes.headline: Committee moved to work toward vacating the aging, ill-suited TC Pasos office building.
minutes.summary: The board heard a presentation on the new second school resource officer and comfort-dog Hank, then spent most of the meeting on facilities and money: the TC Pasos building's deficit and poor condition, FY26 budget priorities including whether to move health insurance out of the school budget, and school committee goals emphasizing facilities and financial stability. Several routine votes passed (minutes, a LEAF nomination, a one-day Spain-trip date change, facilities report, a batch of third-read policies) and the meeting closed by moving into executive session for non-union personnel/collective-bargaining matters.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of August 16, 2024 and September 4, 2024
Nominate Ms. Brazowski as school committee representative to LEAF (Lunenburg education accelerator foundation)
Allow the Spain trip to start one day earlier to reduce costs
Accept the facilities and grounds update report
Adjourn to executive session for strategy sessions/negotiations and collective bargaining with non-union personnel

budget_items.what_was_said: The department said it will request additional funds for Hank's care and training per CBA/FLSA guidelines in the FY26 budget; a member later cited a separate figure for what a second dog would cost the town.
The interim town manager reported a deficit in the TC Pasos operational account that has since been eliminated by transfers from other facility accounts.
The town manager's memo stated the school department, including the before/after school program, is current on rent and operational responsibilities for the building.

budget_items.topic: Leasing space vs. staying at TC Pasos
budget_items.what_was_said: A member questioned whether exploring leased space made sense given the relatively small amount paid for the after-school program.
Airfare rose well above the original per-traveler estimate; shifting the trip one day earlier was said to save each traveler an amount, and two parent-travelers a larger combined amount.

budget_items.topic: FY26 budget - moving healthcare line to the town
budget_items.what_was_said: A member proposed removing the healthcare cost line from the school budget and placing it with the town-wide municipal insurance pool, arguing the district has no control over that pool and it would let the school budget be finalized earlier.

budget_items.topic: Health insurance cost per full-time position
budget_items.what_was_said: A member cited the added benefit cost of converting a part-time position to full-time as a reason department budgets should carry their own health insurance line.

budget_items.topic: Proposed high-deductible health plan / HSA option
budget_items.what_was_said: A member presented a proposal to offer employees an optional high-deductible health plan with a health savings account, saying it could lower premiums for both the town and employees.
The budget task force reported potential annual savings from changing how warrants are mailed, though it would require a charter update.
A member joked about looking for savings equivalent to a large unexplained gap in the town's finances, inviting resident input to the budget task force.

The DPW director's response explained Chapter 90 funds may buy trucks over a certain gross vehicle weight but not seasonal/maintenance equipment, and that DPW will separately seek capital funds for new trucks.

decisions.decision: Superintendent directed to explore options (including Turkey Hill space, leasing, or splitting offices) for moving central administration out of the TC Pasos building.
Committee will not cut the district's two BCBA positions in the FY26 budget planning.
Superintendent to bring two or three budget scenarios to the committee no later than the first meeting in December.
Healthcare line-item relocation question tabled for now; will be revisited during the FY26 budget/healthcare discussion.
Committee agreed to drop proposed goal four and to word-smith goal three (communication) further before adopting the FY26 school committee goals.
School committee goal on facilities will focus specifically on TC Pasos, Turkey Hill, and the turf field rather than all district facility needs.

what_happened.line: Committee directed the superintendent to explore moving central administration out of the TC Pasos building, citing its condition and an account deficit.
Superintendent will bring two or three FY26 budget scenarios to the committee no later than the first December meeting.
Committee said it will not cut the district's two BCBA positions in FY26 budget planning.
A proposal to move the health insurance line out of the school budget and into the town's municipal pool was tabled for the FY26 budget discussion.
Members narrowed a proposed facilities goal to TC Pasos, Turkey Hill, and the turf field and dropped another goal, without formally adopting FY26 goals.

why_it_matters: Where central administration is housed touches a building account residents' taxes cover, and any move to Turkey Hill or leased space would run through the FY26 budget or a future capital request.
Whether health insurance stays in the school budget or moves to the town's pool changes what a resident sees when the school budget comes up for a vote, without changing what the insurance costs.
The board's commitment to keep both BCBA positions is a signal about which special-education services it intends to protect as it builds FY26 budget scenarios.
watch_next: FY26 budget scenarios, due to the committee no later than the first School Committee meeting in December 2024
Formal adoption of the FY26 school committee goals, once goal three's wording is finalized

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the core actions of the night — the LEAF nomination, the facilities report acceptance, the third-read policies, and the general shape of the TC Pasos and comfort-dog discussions — but our minutes are built from misheard captions (names and several policy/dollar figures) while the official minutes are a hand-written narrative that omits most dollar figures and several decisions (BCBA staffing, budget-scenario timeline, specific goal wording) that our recording-based minutes captured. The single item most worth checking is the Spain trip vote and the third-read policy list, where the official record shows a different vote composition (an abstention) and a different set of policy numbers than ours does.
